Share on X Telegram Actors with Nigerian heritage have long had a place in the international entertainment industry, with several of them building successful careers in Hollywood and beyond. From award-winning performers and blockbuster stars to familiar faces on popular streaming platforms, these entertainers have made their mark on screens around the world. Here are 10 internationally recognised actors and actresses with Nigerian roots.
The British actor came into the spotlight after playing Finn in the Star Wars sequel trilogy. Born in London to Nigerian parents of Yoruba descent, Boyega has also featured in Attack the Block, The Woman King and They Cloned Tyrone. Boyega won a Golden Globe for his performance in Steve McQueen’s Small Axe anthology.
Born in London to Igbo Nigerian parents, Ejiofor is one of the most famous actors of Nigerian descent in international cinema. He received an Academy Award nomination for his performance in 12 Years a Slave. His other notable credits include Doctor Strange, The Martian and The Boy Who Harnessed the Wind.
Oyelowo, who is recognised as British-American, was born in Oxford to Nigerian parents and spent part of his childhood in Lagos. He is mostly celebrated for portraying civil rights leader Martin Luther King Jr. in Selma. His other credits include The Butler, Queen of Katwe, Silo and Lawmen: Bass Reeves.
The award-winning British actress and singer was born in London to Nigerian parents. Erivo achieved international repute for portraying abolitionist Harriet Tubman in Harriet, a performance that earned her an Academy Award nomination. Following that, she took on the role of Elphaba in the film adaptation of Wicked, further cementing her status as an international star.
Edebiri is an American actress, comedian and writer. She has become one of the most recognisable young faces in television. Born in Boston to a Nigerian father and Barbadian mother, Edebiri gained widespread recognition for playing Sydney Adamu in the hit series The Bear. Her performance earned her an Emmy, a Golden Globe and other key industry awards. She also voiced Envy in Pixar’s Inside Out 2.
Born in Zaria, Nigeria, to Yoruba parents, Mosaku relocated to Manchester, England, as a young child. She has built an impressive international career, with appearances in Fantastic Beasts and Where to Find Them, Marvel’s Loki and Deadpool & Wolverine. Her performance in the 2025 horror film Sinners earned her a BAFTA Award and an Academy Award nomination.
Idris, who is recognised as British, was born in Peckham, London, to a Nigerian mother. He became widely known for playing Franklin Saint in the crime drama Snowfall, a role that helped establish him as a leading television actor. Idris subsequently featured alongside Brad Pitt in the 2025 racing blockbuster F1, bringing him to an even wider international audience.
Born in Boston to Nigerian parents of Igbo descent, Aduba is mostly known for playing the part of Suzanne Warren, popularly known as Crazy Eyes, in Netflix’s Orange Is the New Black. Her performance earned her two Primetime Emmy Awards for the same role. She subsequently won a third Emmy for portraying politician Shirley Chisholm in the FX series Mrs. America, bringing her total to three Emmy Awards.
Born in London to Nigerian parents, the British actor has enjoyed a long career cutting across film and television. He is popular for playing Mr Eko in Lost and Simon Adebisi in Oz. His film credits include The Mummy Returns, The Bourne Identity, Thor: The Dark World and Suicide Squad.
The British actress was born in London to a Nigerian father and a British Jewish mother. She received an Academy Award nomination for her portrayal of Tatiana Rusesabagina in Hotel Rwanda. Her other screen credits include The Secret Life of Bees, Death on the Nile and the television series Ratched. Okonedo also won a Tony Award for her performance in the Broadway revival of A Raisin in the Sun.
